html:
The long war, from 535 to 554, in which Justinian's empire took Italy back from the Ostrogoths. The Ostrogothic kingdom had been founded by Theoderic; the murder of his daughter Amalasuntha in 535 gave Justinian his excuse.

It went in two phases:

  • 535 to 540: Belisarius took Sicily, Naples and Rome, held Rome through a year-long siege, and captured Ravenna in 540.
  • 541 to 554: the Gothic king Totila won back most of Italy, even retaking Rome. Narses finally beat him at the Battle of Taginae in 552, then crushed the last Goths and a Frankish invasion.

The war came on top of the plague and left Italy ruined: cities sacked, farms abandoned, the Senate gone. Justinian's settlement of 554, the Pragmatic Sanction, did not last. In 568 the Lombards invaded and took most of the peninsula, and Italy would not be united again until the 19th century.
